security_audit.summary: Most Ruby or shell backtick detections are markdown formatting false positives, but several spans contain real runnable npx commands. The skill also uses a hosted image API, hidden agent configuration paths, and a dynamic next-command flow that require user approval and stronger safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions for image-skill and skills commands, and document release provenance for the recommended commands.
Do not tell agents to run data.next_command directly. Require user confirmation and validate generated commands against a narrow allowlist.
Make global installation optional, remove automatic yes from default examples, and explain which agent files may be modified.
Document what images, prompts, outputs, job records, and URLs are uploaded or retained before any command is run.
Use explicit workspace-local paths where possible and provide cleanup steps for .agent-home, .codex, and .agents state.

content.user_title: Edit Images With Hosted AI Models
content.value_statement: Image editing agents need reliable tools without provider setup. This skill guides hosted image edits, variations, cost checks, and durable result links.
actual_capabilities: Runs guided image edit commands through the image-skill CLI.
Supports image-to-image edits, variations, restyling, transforms, and repairs.
Uses a hosted runtime instead of local model servers or provider API keys.
Requests cost limits and JSON output for edit jobs.
Returns durable hosted media URLs, recoverable jobs, and cost receipts.
Provides feedback guidance when a needed capability is missing.
limitations: Requires network access to the Image Skill hosted service.
May spend credits when media generation is allowed.
Depends on the models and policies supported by Image Skill.
Can modify local agent skill configuration during installation.

use_cases.title: Product Image Cleanup
use_cases.description: Replace backgrounds, repair artifacts, or restyle product images while keeping the main subject consistent.

use_cases.title: Creative Variation Review
use_cases.description: Generate controlled image variations with explicit prompts and cost limits for fast concept comparison.

use_cases.title: Agent Media Workflow
use_cases.description: Run recoverable hosted image jobs that return links, receipts, and structured results for later agent handoff.
use_cases.target_user: Developers using Claude, Codex, or Claude Code

prompt_templates.title: Basic Background Edit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner image edit with one clear change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-edit to replace the background of this image with a clean studio setting. Keep the subject, pose, and colors unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Create Style Variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-edit to create three variations of this image in a premium editorial style. Keep the composition recognizable and return the result links.

prompt_templates.title: Controlled Repair With Budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced edit with constraints and spend control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-edit to remove visible artifacts and repair the damaged area. Set a low per-image cost limit and show the estimated spend before creating images.

prompt_templates.title: Workflow Recovery and Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced agent handoff after a missing capability or failed edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-edit to recover the last job for this image. If the requested model feature is unavailable, file feedback with the attempted command and missing capability.

output_examples.input: Replace the background of a product photo while preserving the product edges.
output_examples.output: The result includes a hosted edited image link, a job reference, and a cost receipt for the completed edit.

output_examples.input: Create several restyled variations of a campaign image for review.
output: A set of variation links is returned for comparison.
The response notes the model used and the estimated or actual media cost.
The job can be recovered later by another agent.

output_examples.input: Try an edit that the hosted model does not support yet.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a fallback for the missing capability and records structured feedback for Image Skill.

best_practices: Start with the guide command and review readiness, missing inputs, and estimated cost before creating images.
Use explicit edit prompts that name what should change and what must stay unchanged.
Review hosted URL and retention expectations before uploading sensitive or private images.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated next commands without user approval and command review.
Do not upload confidential images unless the hosted processing policy is acceptable.
Do not use global installation commands when a workspace-local setup is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It is focused on image-to-image edits, variations, restyling, transforms, and repairs.

faq.question: Does it require provider API keys?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses the Image Skill hosted runtime instead of user-supplied provider credentials.

faq.question: Can it run without network access?
faq.answer: No. The workflow depends on hosted Image Skill services and API endpoints.

faq.question: Can it control generation cost?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include guide mode and per-image estimated cost limits.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review the command, package version, upload behavior, cost estimate, and hosted media retention policy.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code agent workflows.
